content_units: Movie Night Shortlist for Four
A balanced mix of clever sci-fi, mystery, and adventure with no graphic gore, all under 130 minutes, and with several picks that work well for ages 11 and 14.
Ranked Watch Options

Option 1:   Arrival (2016, 116 min)     A linguist is recruited to communicate with mysterious alien visitors whose arrival may change humanity’s understanding of time.     Mood:   Thoughtful, awe-filled
-   Why it fits:   Smart, emotional sci-fi with mystery at its core, tense but not gory, and excellent for a group that likes discussing ideas afterward.
Option 2:   Source Code (2011, 93 min)     A soldier relives the same train explosion repeatedly to identify the bomber and prevent a larger attack.     Mood:   Tense, puzzle-box
-   Why it fits:   Fast, clever, and easy to get into, with mystery-thriller energy and sci-fi mechanics that stay accessible.
Option 3:   Edge of Tomorrow (2014, 113 min)     An untrained military officer caught in a time loop must learn to survive an alien war one day at a time.     Mood:   Adrenaline, witty
-   Why it fits:   Inventive sci-fi adventure with strong momentum, humor, and action intensity without graphic gore.
Option 4:   Super 8 (2011, 112 min)     A group of kids filming a movie witness a train crash and uncover a dangerous secret in their small town.     Mood:   Nostalgic, suspenseful
-   Why it fits:   Mystery-adventure with sci-fi elements and a younger cast, making it one of the better family-friendly picks for ages 11 and 14.
Option 5:   The Martian (2015, 144 min)     An astronaut stranded on Mars uses science, humor, and ingenuity to survive while Earth races to bring him home.     Mood:   Uplifting, brainy
-   Why it fits:   Excellent clever sci-fi and very crowd-pleasing, but it runs over your 130-minute cap, so treat this as a near-match backup only.
Option 6:   Enola Holmes (2020, 123 min)     Sherlock Holmes’s younger sister follows clues across London to solve a disappearance while outsmarting adults around her.     Mood:   Playful, brisk
-   Why it fits:   Light mystery-adventure, family-friendly, and easy for mixed ages without losing the cleverness.
Option 7:   Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse (2018, 117 min)     Brooklyn teen Miles Morales teams up with other Spider-heroes to stop a threat unraveling reality.     Mood:   Energetic, uplifting
-   Why it fits:   A highly inventive adventure with sci-fi flavor, visually exciting, funny, and one of the safest great options for ages 11 and 14.
Option 8:   National Treasure (2004, 131 min)     A historian-treasure hunter races to decode clues hidden in American history before his rivals do.     Mood:   Fun, crowd-pleasing
-   Why it fits:   Mystery-adventure comfort watch with broad appeal and no gore, though it is just over your runtime target.
Best Fits by Your Priorities
-   Best overall:     Arrival   — smartest match for clever sci-fi + mystery, under runtime, and mature without being graphic.
-   Best fast-paced pick:     Source Code   — shortest, most efficient crowd-pleaser.
-   Best adventure pick:     Edge of Tomorrow   — strongest action-adventure energy while staying clever.
-   Best family-friendly picks:     Super 8  ,   Enola Holmes  , and   Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse  .
Viewing Notes for Your Group
A few close-call runtime notes affected the list:
-   Fully within your rules:   Arrival, Source Code, Edge of Tomorrow, Super 8, Enola Holmes, Into the Spider-Verse
-   Near-match backups:   National Treasure (131 min), The Martian (144 min)
If you want the safest single choice for all four viewers,   Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse   is the easiest yes. If you want the most discussion-worthy pick, choose   Arrival  .
